children: New Zealand stocks lost 130 points, or 0.9%, to close at 13,787 on Tuesday, touching their lowest level since August 17 and erasing gains in the previous session, mainly weighed down by industrials, real estate, consumer discretionary, and consumer staples.
The broader index tracked a decline on Wall Street overnight as rising oil prices raised inflation concerns amid escalating Middle East tensions.
Traders were cautious ahead of the RBNZ's monetary policy decision this week, with the market expecting the central bank to raise interest rates by 25 bps after raising them in May.
Traders continued to assess the government's decision to delay fuel excise rises from January 1, 2027, ahead of the general election, which is scheduled to be held in November 2026.
Among the top decliners were Auckland International Airport (-3.2%), Ebos Group (-1.9%), A2 Milk (-1.6%), Infratil (-1.1%), and Contact Energy (-0.8%).

title: New Zealand Equities Close 0.9% Lower
